assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting and then observing the quantum spin Hall state reorganised how condensed-matter physics classifies phases: a topological invariant rather than a broken symmetry distinguishes insulators, with protected edge transport as a measurable consequence. The idea is original, conceptually clean and has spawned a very large field.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theory (Z2 invariant, spin-orbit-gapped graphene); Molenkamp's group delivered the HgTe/CdTe observation after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not a credited name. Hasan's 3D topological-insulator work is a separate contribution; a three-person prize is defensible but leaves out parts of the field.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups and materials, with a stable interpretation, and now textbook material. Timing is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the BHZ proposal and the 3D topological-insulator discovery should be credited alongside the 2D result.
The 2016 prize already covered topological phase transitions, so the committee must judge how much new ground this adds.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model's electroweak sector and is among the most consequential measurements in physics. The 2013 prize recognised the theory, so the experimental discovery has no prize yet.
assessment.attribution: The discovery rests on collaborations of thousands. The credited individuals were leaders and architects of ATLAS and CMS, but the choice of three from four named people is a leadership-based judgement, not a statement about who made the decisive measurement. This is the hardest allocation problem on the list.
assessment.maturity: The discovery has been confirmed with extensive follow-up on couplings and spin-parity, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Fair attribution to individuals within very large collaborations is unresolved and may conflict with the prize statutes.
I rely on general knowledge of the leadership roles and have not verified them independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling between superconducting qubits and microwave resonators routine, giving the readout and control architecture on which superconducting quantum processors are built. Its influence on quantum technology and on basic quantum optics on a chip is large.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf with others proposed and demonstrated the architecture in 2004; Steven Girvin and other co-authors of the original theory are not on this list, and the broader credit is shared with the qubit-circuit community. A three-person configuration is plausible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many laboratories and in commercial devices. Recognition is timely given the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, although that recent award may make the committee wary of staying in the same area.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with the 2025 prize topic and with Girvin and other co-authors.
How the committee weighs engineering impact against fundamental discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire engineering of strongly correlated matter. It is original and has had broad impact on the study of correlated electrons.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental observations (with Cao and others, who are not credited here). The theory-plus-experiment pairing yields a natural three-person configuration, although early-career experimentalists are omitted.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across several groups and moire platforms, though the nature of the superconductivity and of the correlated states is still debated. The field is young and the interpretation is not fully stable.
uncertainties: Credit for Pablo Jarillo-Herrero's co-workers and for other independent theory and experiments is not captured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned the no-cloning theorem and entanglement into a practical cryptographic principle and helped found quantum information science. The idea is original and conceptually clear, and it links foundations to technology.
assessment.attribution: BB84 (Bennett and Brassard) and the entanglement-based E91 protocol (Ekert) are the standard foundational contributions, giving a natural trio. Other protocols and the later experimental demonstrations are not covered.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally demonstrated and deployed in field trials and satellite links; the foundations are solid, although practical security under real devices remains a concern. The 2022 prize on Bell tests overlaps in subject but covered different work.
uncertainties: Whether the physics, rather than computer-science or engineering, character of the contribution suffices for a physics prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, via the magic-wavelength idea, reach unmatched fractional stability and accuracy and enable tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The conceptual step and its metrological outcome are clear and important.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and Ye's group drove its experimental performance to record levels. The two-person attribution is clean, although ion clocks and other groups also contributed to optical-clock progress.
assessment.maturity: The clocks are demonstrated and used in redefinition planning for the second; this is mature, and the 2005 prize to Hall and Hänsch recognised the frequency comb, which is a related but different contribution.
uncertainties: Overlap with the optical clock and frequency-comb prizes.
Credit to groups building other clock types (ion clocks) is outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation defines a universality class of nonequilibrium growth with exact connections to random matrix theory. The theory of 1986 and the later experimental confirmation in liquid-crystal turbulence give a deep and widely relevant statistical-physics result that I know well from my own field.
assessment.attribution: Kardar, Parisi and Zhang wrote the original equation; Parisi is absent from the credited names and he has already received the 2021 prize. The mathematical exact solutions (Tracy-Widom statistics, Sasamoto, Spohn, Amir, Corwin and others) are not credited either, so the allocation is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Theoretical status is solid, and the experiment of Takeuchi and Sano gives independent confirmation. The impact on experiments is more limited than for other candidates.
uncertainties: Absence of Giorgio Parisi and the exact-solution contributors from the credited names.
Narrower experimental reach than other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method and message-passing algorithms for random constraint satisfaction connected spin-glass theory to computer science and inference, and they underlie current analyses of high-dimensional learning problems. This is close to my own interests, although the foundation rests partly on Parisi's replica work already recognised in 2021.
assessment.attribution: Mézard and Zecchina developed the cavity method for optimisation problems and survey propagation; Montanari's work extends it to inference and compressed sensing. Parisi, Mézard and Virasoro's earlier spin-glass work forms an overlapping credit unit.
assessment.maturity: Many rigorous results (e.g. for the satisfiability threshold) confirm the picture, and applications to learning are active. Recognition is plausible but the practical impact is still developing.
uncertainties: Novelty relative to the 2021 prize for disordered systems.
Whether the work is considered physics or applied mathematics and computer science.
